map.title: [Wayfinder Map] First-time manager dashboard usability
map.body:
## Destination

Agree manager-facing dashboard UX specification from blind persona click-through: confident deadline decisions, interpretable comparisons, deliberate scouting handoff and chip experiments. Complete when observed questions resolved into reviewable behavior decisions; implementation follows separately.

## Notes

2026-10-09 desktop UI-only audit; no application source inspection by personas. Deadline and strategy agents direct; scout commands relayed by root because scout browser unavailable. Evidence archived locally in anti-slop/audit-002-2026-10-09.md; reproducible observations included in each child. Antislop After; preserve DESIGN.md. Consult Wayfinder, antislop core/UI/human/copy, grilling and domain-modeling as relevant. P1/P2/P3 denote user-impact triage. Open children are decision questions, not automatically approved changes. No real FPL submission or live refresh.

## Decisions so far

None. Audit observations are evidence, not resolved product decisions.

## Not yet specified

- Responsive, full keyboard, screen-reader and 200% zoom experience after chosen workflows.
- Performance and failure recovery under a single isolated session; intermediate reruns excluded from bug claims.
- Detailed rollout order and implementation scope after decisions.
- One-off view-preference save warning; reproduce before diagnosing.

## Out of scope

Scoring-model changes, Champion/Candidate research, solver correctness claims, official FPL transfers, deployment, new model training, cosmetic redesign without decision evidence.

tickets.title: [P1] What must a manager see before acting at the deadline?
tickets.body:
## Question

Which compact planner summary establishes deadline readiness and next action without scrolling through the whole squad?

## Observed evidence

Deadline reviewer: only Start: GW6 · upcoming deadline; costs and both score metrics below XI and bench. No absolute deadline/timezone/last-refresh metadata visible in inspected planner.

## Proposed adjustment for discussion

Prototype compact decision summary containing deadline/timezone, data age, active policy, captain/vice, transfers, hit cost, bank and lineup readiness. Preserve full squad inspection.

## Decision acceptance

First-time manager can state upcoming deadline, data age, active plan and costs from initial planner view. Metadata has explicit unavailable/stale states.

tickets.title: [P1] How should managers compare transfer policies with rolling a transfer?
tickets.body:
## Question

Which shared metrics and horizon explain Optimal, No Hit and Conservative against a no-transfer baseline?

## Observed evidence

GW6 Optimal: lineup after hits 53.93 / Expected GW Score 59.41, hit minus 4. No Hit 55.98 / 61.43. Conservative 54.28 / 59.12. No horizon benefit or hold baseline visible in inspected planner. Lower immediate score does not prove solver bug.

## Proposed adjustment for discussion

Agree same-horizon comparison, no-transfer baseline and readable justification for hit or sacrifice this week. Explain difference between Expected GW Score, lineup projection and optimization objective.

## Decision acceptance

Manager can compare all three policies and hold baseline without replacing current draft; decisions state horizon, costs, transfer count and metric definitions.

tickets.title: [P2] How should policy preview differ from adopting a saved draft?
tickets.body:
## Question

How can a manager preview another policy while knowing exactly which plan is active and when edits will be replaced?

## Observed evidence

Deadline and strategist independently selected No Hit while active headline remained Optimal; Use selected scenario applies it in second step. Controls work; pending state explanation unclear.

## Proposed adjustment for discussion

Prototype active/pending labels, comparison preview and explicit adoption with manual-edit safeguard.

## Decision acceptance

Selecting policy never implies active-plan change; current and preview labels remain distinguishable through reruns; adoption and discard/recovery paths clear.

tickets.title: [P2] How should player availability and fixture difficulty be presented?
tickets.body:
## Question

What plain-language risk and fixture summary helps a first-time manager interpret projections without internal identifiers?

## Observed evidence

Haaland and Mbeumo: Availability:a; Gibbs-White:a ·100%; João Pedro:d ·75%, Knee injury - 75% chance of playing inside inspector. Fixture TOT(H)1.75 merges unexplained decimal into fixture. Visible xp_* table headers.

## Proposed adjustment for discussion

Prototype translated availability, concise card-level injury risk, separately labelled difficulty with meaning/direction and expandable component explanation.

## Decision acceptance

Manager can explain availability, injury information and fixture difficulty; missing data distinguished from fit/zero; technical component names optional.

tickets.title: [P2] How should scouting comparisons lead into a transfer draft?
tickets.body:
## Question

How should manager compare two targets then intentionally prepare selected target in Transfer Planner while keeping Explorer What-If separate?

## Observed evidence

Scout-directed root clicks: MID budget £8, inspect Mbeumo then Gibbs-White, Back to Explorer, Transfer Planner. Dialogs close correctly; no compare/shortlist/handoff in tested path. Planner loads saved recommendation without target. Scout browser unavailable, relayed workflow disclosed.

## Proposed adjustment for discussion

Prototype side-by-side shortlist and explicit prepare-in-planner action with outgoing-player choice and draft review. Preserve isolation of What-If and official squad.

## Decision acceptance

Two candidates share same horizon and definitions; chosen target carries into reviewed draft preparation without implicit save, solver run or official submission.

tickets.title: [P2] What validation belongs before submitting a chip experiment?
tickets.body:
## Question

How should advanced strategy distinguish a legal fixed chip schedule from alternative chip dates, and warn before submission?

## Observed evidence

Strategist selected Wildcard GW8 and Bench Boost GW8 simultaneously; no inline warning; Run advanced solve available. No solve submitted, so backend handling unknown. Start GW6 / horizon 3 correctly restricts choices to GW6-8.

## Proposed adjustment for discussion

Decide immediate validation/exclusion of occupied date, warning placement, legal alternatives and whether action blocks submission.

## Decision acceptance

Conflict visible beside affected controls before solve; manager can distinguish fixed schedule from alternative experiments. Verify backend errors later without asserting current solver accepts conflicts.

tickets.title: [P2] What explanations make advanced strategy inputs usable?
tickets.body:
## Question

Which plain-language presets, units and examples let manager tune future weeks, hits, bank and bench rationally?

## Observed evidence

Visible defaults: decay 0.85, Free Transfer value 1.50, Bank value 0.08, bench weights 0.21 / 0.06. No visible examples/units. Methodology covers projections, not Conservative/policy weights; wildcard research search empty.

## Proposed adjustment for discussion

Prototype control-specific examples and consequences, plain policy definitions, sensible presets and contextual guidance.

## Decision acceptance

Manager can explain horizon 3 means GW6-8, decay, bank/free-transfer value and bench influence before changing inputs; projected outcomes remain separate from scoring-model explanations.

tickets.title: [P3] Should advanced experiment settings survive reload?
tickets.body:
## Question

Which advanced inputs persist, and what recovery or explicit session-only warning should accompany reload and concurrent-draft protection?

## Observed evidence

WC/BB GW8 reset to Unbooked after reload; saved draft recovered. Separate-experiment caption does not disclose input lifetime. View preference could not be saved observed once; not independently reproduced. Concurrent draft guard worked.

## Proposed adjustment for discussion

Decide session-only disclosure versus persistent/exportable experiment setup, save feedback and recovery. Investigate one-off warning only if reproduced.

## Decision acceptance

Document lifetime beside setup; reload behavior matches decision; user sees meaningful recovery after failed preference write; concurrent guard preserved.
